summary: Read-only v2.0 quality audit of digitalharm.org: accuracy, navigation, competitive gaps, clarity/a11y, external-link integrity -> prioritized punch-list
logs: Audit complete: 34 findings (P0:1 P1:8 P2:9 P3:16) across 5/5 dimensions

result.synthesisMarkdown:
I'll synthesize the 34 findings into a clean v2.0 punch-list. Let me work through the deduplication and prioritization. ## Executive summary digitalharm.org is in exceptionally strong shape: the accuracy audit found **zero P0/P1 factual errors** (every crisis number, legal status, and statistic verifies against primary sources), navigation has no orphans, and every crisis/help link is live. The single highest-leverage opportunity is a format gap, not a content gap — there is **no interactive triage tool**, so a panicked 2am user must read prose to self-route while every leading competitor offers a guided front door. The most impactful content/UX work for v2.0 clusters into four threads: build the triage router, close the **safety-cluster cross-link gaps** (especially the time-critical `/sextortion` page, which can't reach removal tools or legal rights inline), fix two **WCAG AA contrast/semantics barriers** that degrade help exactly at peak stress, and name the **porn-science skeptic studies** the site's own editorial standard already promises. One genuine link defect (a redirecting Stanford source) and a handful of accuracy polish items round out the list. ## P0 — fix immediately **No materially false claims and no broken crisis paths.** This is a strong signal. The accuracy audit verified every crisis/help number (NCMEC 1-800-843-5678, Stop It Now US 1-888-773-8368 / UK 0808 1000 900, RAINN 1-800-656-4673, CCRI 1-844-878-2274, Crisis Text Line 741741, 988), every enacted-vs-proposed legal distinction, and every headline statistic against primary sources. The links audit confirmed every crisis/help URL is live and canonical. There are no URL-only orphans and every page carries the global header + footer, so there are no absolute dead ends. One item is filed at **P0 severity by the gaps auditor but it is an enhancement, not a defect** — there is nothing broken to fix immediately. It is carried as the top item in P1 below so it is not lost: - **No interactive triage/decision tool exists anywhere on the site.** This is the clearest gap between "best encyclopedia in the field" (which the site already is) and "best resource on the planet." It is net-new work, so it belongs in the planned v2.0 build rather than an emergency hotfix. See P1 #1. ## P1 — high value for v2.0 Ordered by impact. Findings merged across dimensions where they overlap. ### 1. Build a "Get help in 60 seconds" interactive triage router **Source: gaps (P0-severity), reinforced by clarity's crisis-flow strengths.** **Location:** new client route, e.g. `/help-now`; routes into existing `/sextortion`, `/remove-images`, `/for-reporting`, `/for-offenders`, `/get-help`, `/for-parents`. **Why:** The only two client components in the repo are `components/search-box.tsx` and `components/content-notice.tsx` — there is no branching "what do I do" flow. NCMEC Take It Down, eSafety, and Thorn all convert a panicked user with a guided front door; this site makes them read prose to self-route. **Action:** Build a lightweight, no-login, client-side branching flow (3–4 questions: *Is the person depicted under 18? Are images already shared? Is there an active threat/extortion? Which country?*). Make it a **router into existing pages** (respects the "no parallel guide" rule), e.g.: - minor image abuse → Take It Down + `/remove-images` - adult NCII → StopNCII / CCRI 1-844-878-2274 - sextortion in progress → `/sextortion` (don't pay / don't delete / screenshot / report) + 988 - worried about own attraction → `/for-offenders` + Stop It Now US 1-888-773-8368 / UK 0808 1000 900 - child saw porn → `/for-parents#by-age` - found CSAM → CyberTipline + do-not-download warning Register the route in `lib/search.ts` PAGE_REGISTRY and `sitemap.ts`, and give safety-critical destinations the recommended search intent-boost. ### 2. Close the safety-cluster cross-links — start with `/sextortion` **Source: navigation (three merged findings: sextortion P1, laws P2, organizations↔laws P2).** This is the highest-value navigation cluster; treat the sub-items as one work package. - **`/sextortion` (most urgent — `app/sextortion/page.tsx`):** the most time-sensitive page on the site does **not** link to `/remove-images`, `/laws`, or `/organizations`, even though `/remove-images` already links back to it. Add inline links to `/remove-images` (the removal step), `/laws` (your 48-hour takedown right + restitution), and `/organizations` (who can help / report). Makes sextortion↔remove-images bidirectional. - **`/laws` (`app/laws/page.tsx`):** links only to platform/compliance audiences + stats; never back into the survivor journey. Add links to `/remove-images` and `/sextortion` ("how to exercise these rights") and to `/organizations` (who enforces / who helps). - **`/organizations` (`app/organizations/page.tsx`):** add a `/laws` link and a `/sextortion` link (for survivors who land here first). Net result: the sextortion ↔ remove-images ↔ laws ↔ organizations cluster becomes bidirectional. ### 3. Fix the `--subtle` contrast failure on load-bearing safety text **Source: clarity (P1), with the laws-badge emphasis issue (P2) merged in — same root token.** **Location:** `app/globals.css:8` (`--subtle` `#8a8f9a`). Load-bearing uses: `app/remove-images/page.tsx:209` (ToolCard situation labels), `app/laws/page.tsx:34` (Proposed-not-law badge) and `:184` (statute dates), `app/csam-statistics/page.tsx:214` (source/year line). **Why:** `#8a8f9a` is only ~3.0–3.2:1 — below WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1 for small text. It is applied to the exact cues a distressed/low-vision user must read to route themselves: the remove-images ToolCard labels ("The image is of someone who was **UNDER 18**" / "**ADULT 18+**") and the laws "Proposed — not law" badge. **Action:** Darken `--subtle` to ~`#6c7280` (≥4.5:1 on the off-white bg) and re-verify, **or** switch load-bearing <18.66px text off `text-subtle` to `text-muted` (`#5b6577`, 5.5:1, already passing). Separately, make the **"Proposed — not law" badge visually louder** than the Enacted badge (heavier-weight/solid fill; the page's whole purpose is stopping readers from treating proposed bills as law, yet this badge is currently the weakest). Keep the explicit text label in all cases. ### 4. Convert the sextortion "three rules" to a real list **Source: clarity (P1).** **Location:** `app/sextortion/page.tsx:38-47` (hero crisis callout). **Why:** The single most urgent instruction set on the site (Don't pay / Stop responding but don't delete / Tell someone and report) is one run-on `

` with fake inline "1. 2. 3." bolding. It can't be skimmed step-by-step and a screen reader announces it as one undifferentiated paragraph — the worst possible format for an acute-panic reader. **Action:** Convert to a real `

    ` (three stacked `
  1. ` rows) inside the existing crisis-colored box, mirroring the correct `
      ` already used lower on the same page. ### 5. Give external links unique accessible names; hide the decorative arrow **Source: clarity (P1).** **Location:** all 8 pages. Examples: `app/organizations/page.tsx:127-129` ("Visit" ×22 orgs), `app/prevention/page.tsx:167` ("Learn more" ×6), `app/laws/page.tsx:186-188` ("Primary source" ×10), `app/csam-statistics/page.tsx:241`, `app/for-parents/page.tsx:330`. **Why:** Screen-reader users navigating by links list hear "Visit, Visit, Visit…" / "Primary source, Primary source…" with no way to distinguish destinations; the decorative ↗ glyph is also announced as "north east arrow" on every link. **Action:** Add a unique `aria-label` per link (e.g. `"Visit " + org.name`, `"Primary source for " + law.name`, `"Learn more about " + program.name`). Wrap the arrow glyph in ``. ### 6. Fix the Stanford Internet Observatory source link (only genuine link defect) **Source: links (P1).** **Location:** `app/organizations/page.tsx:65` (SIO org card) and `app/csam-statistics/page.tsx:238` (Sources item backing the page's flagship "Read these numbers responsibly" caveat). Both use `https://cyber.fsi.stanford.edu/io`. **Why:** That URL returns 301 and redirects **off-host** to `https://tip.fsi.stanford.edu/`; SIO was wound down in 2024. On `/csam-statistics` this is the cited primary source for the page's central credibility claim (Pfefferkorn: a "Generative AI"-flagged report is not confirmed AI-CSAM), so the redirect weakens the page's most important caveat. **Action:** Re-point both to a stable, self-resolving URL — ideally the specific publication: `https://cyber.fsi.stanford.edu/publication/how-fix-online-child-exploitation-reporting-system` (verified live) or the Stanford Digital Repository copy `https://purl.stanford.edu/pr592kc5483`. On `/csam-statistics`, also consider relabeling "Stanford Internet Observatory" to its current home (Stanford Cyber Policy Center). ### 7. Name the porn-science skeptic studies the editorial standard already promises **Source: gaps (P1). Confirm with owner — see note.** **Location:** `content/locales/en/report.ts` addiction chapter (extend the existing "gateway hypothesis: evidence and contestation" section) + the existing `/editorial-standards` "How we handle contested science" section. **Why:** The site already has the *scaffold* for even-handedness and names Grubbs / "the skeptics' case," but verified corpus counts show the specific counter-voices are absent: **Prause = 0, Kraus = 0, AASECT = 0, Ferguson = 0** across all content. The neurobiology section presents Voon and Kühn/Gallinat as addiction-supporting with no named rebuttal. For a site whose differentiator vs Fight the New Drug / Covenant Eyes is even-handedness, this is where practice lags the stated standard. **Action:** Add the specific skeptic studies inline (not a new page): Prause et al. 2015 (lower LPP to sexual cues), Steele/Prause 2013 (P300 tracked desire, not hypersexuality), Ley/Prause/Finn 2014 "The Emperor Has No Clothes," Ferguson & Hartley 2022, AASECT 2016 position — paired with the pro-model names already partially present (Brand/I-PACE, Wright, Kraus/Voon/Potenza 2016). **Note:** the SYNTHESIS lists this rebalancing posture as an open editorial question; the editorial-standards page already commits to it, but confirm with the owner before shipping. ### 8. Add a standalone consumer glossary **Source: gaps (P1).** **Location:** new `/glossary` (or `/terminology`); link from report chapters, `/organizations`, `/for-reporting`. **Why:** Terminology rationale (why "CSAM" not "child pornography," attraction-vs-offending) lives only inside `/editorial-standards`; definitions of grooming/sextortion/etc. are scattered. A well-anchored glossary is a durable backlink/authority asset (educators, journalists, courts cite glossaries) and the source material is already assembled. **Action:** Build a glossary anchored on the ECPAT Luxembourg Guidelines with stable per-term anchors + "last verified" dates (CSAM, grooming, sextortion incl. financial sextortion, self-generated content, capping, live-streamed abuse, NCII, hash-matching, CSBD). Register in PAGE_REGISTRY + `sitemap.ts`; consider the build-time check that fails CI if a route lacks a registry entry. ## P2/P3 — backlog **Navigation** - **P2** — `/get-help` is the highest-traffic page but only links onward to `/for-reporting` + `/get-help/bay-area`. Add a "related help / next steps" block linking `/sextortion`, `/remove-images`, `/prevention`, `/apps`, `/organizations`, and `/for-victims` / `/for-offenders` / `/for-parents`. (`app/get-help/page.tsx`) - **P1→treat as P2** — No home path-card for the developer/builder audience, though every other persona has one. Add a card ("I build software / run infrastructure" → `/for-developers` or `/tools`). (`app/page.tsx:146-152`) - **P2** — "Partner affected by a loved one" is named in home CTA (`page.tsx:247`) and the get-help hero but has no card and no destination (folded into `/get-help#families`). Relabel that section to surface partners and point a home affordance at it. - **P3** — Header nav is `hidden md:flex` with no mobile toggle; on phones only logo + search + Get Help show. Add a mobile menu, or at minimum keep a visible "Browse" link (the full index). (`components/site-header.tsx:12-37`) - **P3** — `/citations` has zero in-content internal links (relative dead end); add a few "related" links (`/editorial-standards`, `/csam-statistics`, `/#chapters`). Also `/search` is absent from PAGE_REGISTRY and `/browse` — add it or document the exclusion. (`app/citations/page.tsx`, `lib/search.ts`) - **P3** — Label drift across surfaces for the same routes (`/for-offenders` = "I'm worried about myself" / "For People Seeking Help" / "People seeking help for themselves"; `/for-victims` similar). Pick one canonical label per route and reuse it on home cards, header/footer, `/browse`, search registry. **Gaps / content** - **P2** — `/csam-statistics` is missing a youth-exposure stat group. Add "Exposure & prevalence (youth)": Common Sense Media "Teens and Pornography" (avg first exposure ~12; 54% by 13; 73% have seen porn; 58% accidental) and Childlight "Into the Light" 2024 (~302M / 1 in 8), each year-stamped with primary source. - **P2** — No consumer per-platform app-risk guide (eSafety Guide / Common Sense mold). `/apps` is a protective-tools directory, not a "is Discord/Roblox/Snap safe for my 12-yo and what do I do" reference. Build a filterable per-platform guide (Discord, Roblox, Snapchat, TikTok, Instagram Teen Accounts, YouTube, AI chat/image apps): what it is, risk vector, company age rating, top 1–2 safety settings, how to report/block; tap-by-tap parental-control setup can live here too. - **P3** — Cross-surface US/Finland prevention programs onto the action page: add "Help Wanted" (Johns Hopkins Moore Center) and ReDirection (Protect Children, Finland) to `/for-offenders` pre-charge steps + "Where to start" grid (currently only on the `/prevention` explainer). - **P3** — Anchor Thorn "Safety by Design for Generative AI" (+ signatory list + 2025 progress report) as the actionable standard in `/for-developers` and `/for-tech-ceos`, tied to the existing LAION-5B/Re-LAION coverage. Currently named only in the `/organizations` entry. - **P3** — Localization scaffolded but unbuilt: `content/locales/es/` and `content/locales/zh/` are empty dirs and routing has no `[lang]` segment. Either build out (translate the triage tool + `/for-reporting` + `/sextortion`/`/remove-images` crisis steps to Spanish first) or remove the empty dirs to avoid implying coverage. **Clarity / a11y** - **P2** — Inverted urgency color-coding on `/for-parents`: the top immediate-danger "call 911" box uses amber `warning`, while the lower 988 box uses red `crisis`. Switch the top box to the crisis (red) treatment so the loudest signal matches the most urgent action. (`app/for-parents/page.tsx:43` vs `:209`) - **P2** — Isolated expert jargon raises reading level. Lead plain-then-technical: reverse "iatrogenic" → "treatment can sometimes make things worse (an iatrogenic effect)"; move inline researcher citations (Mokros & Banse; Holper; Mews) to sentence-end/footnote (`app/prevention/page.tsx:201-204`); replace "horizontal platform-governance regime" with "broad platform-rules law" (`app/laws/page.tsx:105`); front-load "digital fingerprint" before "perceptual-hashing" (`app/remove-images/page.tsx:109`). - **P3** — Card tap-target ergonomics: only a short underlined phrase + 12px link is tappable; the large card body is inert and 12px links approach the 44×44px minimum. Make the whole card a click target (wrap in link or stretched-link overlay), pad links to ~44px, and confirm a visible keyboard focus ring. (`app/remove-images/page.tsx:196-218`; card grids in `organizations`/`prevention`) - **P3** — `/remove-images` hero crisis callout doesn't surface 988 (it's only in the last section); add a one-line "if you are in crisis, call or text 988" to the hero to match `/sextortion`. (`app/remove-images/page.tsx:38-44`) **Accuracy polish** (all P3; low/medium confidence — verify before editing) - **P3** — `/csam-statistics:55-60` "NCMEC referred 18.8M+ reports to law enforcement" (2025) cannot be sourced to NCMEC's first-look post or the baseline; verify, then soften or remove the specific number. *(medium)* - **P3** — `/csam-statistics:80` IWF "7,063 realistic enough to be treated as real CSAM" isn't IWF's public phrasing; verify against the IWF 2024 AI-CSAM page or replace with IWF's published framing (~40% Category A; 6,945 / 98% girls). *(low)* - **P3** — `/csam-statistics:105` enticement "+158% vs 2024" — NCMEC's first-look says 156%; align for exactness (and update baseline). *(low)* - **P3** — StopNCII attribution "run by the UK Revenge Porn Helpline" on `organizations:74`, `remove-images:73`, `sextortion:127` — operator of record is SWGfL; tighten to "run by SWGfL (the charity behind the UK Revenge Porn Helpline)." *(high)* - **P3** — `organizations:52` Moore Center "reach" string contains a malformed placeholder "preventationresearch / Moore Center"; replace with the real handle/URL or remove. *(high)* - **P3** — `for-parents:228` ResourceList blurb has literal `minors' intimate images` in a plain JS string (will render the entity verbatim); use a literal apostrophe. *(medium)* **Links** - **P3** — WeProtect GTA `-23` slug (`csam-statistics:237`) is live and correct today but perishable (a `-25` edition exists). No change now; add to the `scripts/check-perishable-citations.ts` watch list. *(high)* ## What is already strong (do not regress) - **Factual accuracy:** zero P0/P1 errors. All crisis numbers, all enacted-vs-proposed legal distinctions (EARN IT + EU CSA Regulation correctly marked PROPOSED; DSA, TAKE IT DOWN Act, REPORT Act, UK OSA, Australia under-16 correctly dated), and all 2024/2025-preliminary statistics verify against NCMEC/IWF/Thorn/congress.gov/EUR-Lex. The page figures and the `FINDINGS-SUMMARY.md` baseline are mutually consistent. The GAI caveat box (Pfefferkorn/Stanford) is responsible. - **External links:** no broken or wrong crisis/help link anywhere (CyberTipline, Take It Down, StopNCII, FBI tips, Childline Report Remove, CCRI, RAINN, all prevention helplines). All legal/authority/org/source links resolve correctly. *(Do not "fix" `tips.fbi.gov` — 403 to bots but live for users — or the Microsoft PhotoDNA link — verified 200; both are correct.)* - **Reachability:** 28 routes, no URL-only orphans, every content page ≤2 clicks from home. `/browse` and `/guides` are near-complete indexes; the search registry enumerates essentially the whole site. Every page has the global header + footer, so no absolute dead ends. Report chapters are well-connected (prev/next + guaranteed `/get-help` fallback). - **Crisis UX & a11y foundation:** warm, explicitly non-shaming tone on the highest-stakes pages; clean h1→h2→h3 with no skips on all 8 pages; jump-nav ToC on every page; the two true emergency pages (`/sextortion`, `/remove-images`) lead with a red crisis callout above any explanation; global skip-link + persistent red "Get Help" button + content-notice. Most contrast tokens are strong (foreground 15:1, accent 6.6:1, crisis 9.7:1). - **Content maturity:** the entire net-new backlog and consolidation waves have essentially shipped. Verified present and good: `/csam-statistics`, `/laws` (Masha's Law/Paroline/AVAA/§2259), `/organizations` (Childlight 302M, Thorn Safety-by-Design), `/editorial-standards` (real "contested science" section), `/prevention` (Moore Center "Help Wanted," Finland ReDirection, **and** the honest "does treatment work?" counterweight citing Mokros & Banse 2019, Holper 2024, Mews 2017), `/remove-images` (restitution + Take It Down/StopNCII/Report Remove/Arachnid), `/sextortion`, `/for-parents` (age-by-age conversations, pre-emptive sextortion script, grooming patterns, device-as-guardrails).
